author.continuation:
Section 24.6 text is written. Body: handbook/parts/p03/structures-definability-and-elementary-maps-w03-p03-006.tex, lines 1-389. Its heading is \chapter, as the packet specifies. It contains: conventions on reducts and named tuples; the elementary amalgam definition; a five-step diagram procedure; Amalgamation into an expansion (thm:p03-w03-p03-006-expansion-amalgamation); the Elementary amalgamation corollary (two clauses); Disjoint amalgamation over an elementary substructure; Amalgamating a family; Existential amalgamation, stated as an equivalence; Models of the universal part; Models of the restricted theory T^L, with a moreover clause; a worked DLO example with non-disjoint and disjoint amalgams over Q; a failure warning, where disjointness fails over a non-elementary common set (one-element predicate); the N/Z example of an embedding that cannot be made elementary; a relationships paragraph; and sources.

Annex: handbook/annex/p03/structures-definability-and-elementary-maps-w03-p03-006.tex, lines 1-428. It gives preliminary facts on reducts, embeddings and quantifier-free formulas, and renaming via Foundation, then 7 annexitems with full proofs: annex:p03-w03-p03-006-expand, -elem, -disjoint, -family, -exist, -univ, -reduct.

author.continuation:
This block closed the listed gaps for units -01 and -02, with every locator checked against the held Fraisse PDF (pp. 363-388) and the Rado page images (pp. 331-337).

Fraisse host:
- The wording on the projection-filter history is corrected. The phrase 'set out differently' comes from the text of Sec. 1.1, not from a footnote.
- New theorem thm:p03-w03-p03-014-arithmetic-types. Part 1: an arithmetic type gets the Theorem IV conclusion, and countably many countable members share a countable host (by downward Lowenheim-Skolem). Part 2: a counterexample built from marked successor chains, with a full annex proof, shows that some arithmetic type fails condition C. This refutes the claim in Sec. 10.1, p. 388, read with the definition of C in Sec. 4.7.

Rado host additions:
- Sec. 1.1: two distinct edges meet in at most one point.
- Sec. 2.1: graphs are one-dimensional complexes.
- Sec. 2.2, n. 4: the Lemma is applied only as 'into'.
- Sec. 3: Theorems 1, 3 and 4 correspond to K_21, K_2l and K_2 and follow from Theorem 5 (thm:p03-w03-p03-014-rado-k2).
- Sec. 4.1: Tarski's cofinality function with the source's own definition, and its equivalence with ordinary cofinality (thm:p03-w03-p03-014-tarski-cf).
- Sec. 4.2: the 'WLOG m initial' remark is reported and shown to fail as a reduction by cardinality (def:p03-w03-p03-014-rado-initial).

Owned annex fixes:
- The amalgam in the K_1 proof wrongly kept a primed copy of the positive point; it no longer does.
- The Lowenheim-Skolem reference now uses the routed label thm:downward-ls.

Checks: unit-compile ok; find_fused_spaces reports no hits; check.py shows no hard finding in the touched files. The only notation-scope findings are pre-existing ones for symbols registered under named P3 Fraisse/Rado scopes.

Remaining:
- The Hodges 1993 ch. 7 presentation, plus MAP-06, is blocked_source.
- Proposed change: the symbols.csv row for \mathrm{cf}(n) should name it Tarski's cofinality function.
- No intake bib was needed; no new keys.

author.continuation:
The assessment said the owned body and annex files were missing. They already existed from an earlier block: body 650 lines and annex 839 lines, covering the canonical extension, iteration, indiscernibles of any ordinal length, and MSS under IS plus LNP. They were extended, not rewritten.

Added this block, each with a full annex proof:
- a compactness lemma for weak L(Q) structures in any vocabulary;
- the MacDowell-Specker theorem for PA, including the derivation in PA of the order facts, IS and LNP;

- an example showing that mu = lambda fails.

- Theorems 6.1.2, 6.1.3, 6.1.5 and 6.1.6. They need sources with full proofs, such as Schmerl 1976 and Schmerl-Shelah 1972.
- Theorem 6.2.2 under the induction scheme alone.

author.continuation:
This block worked through the assigned Morley 1965 gap items (1)-(12), reading the whole held PDF in this session (p. 535 was also rendered to check nn. 22-24).

What was written:
- New body and annex files carry eight results, each with a full annex proof:
  - DLO is categorical in aleph_0 and in no uncountable power.
  - The canonical basis of S(A) has power kappa(A) modulo aleph_0.
  - Morley's Theorem 2.3 holds in every derivative category, and the one-space case is the Cantor-Bendixson derivative.
  - Saturated is equivalent to universal and homogeneous in N(T), for every infinite power.
  - Vaught's limit-power statement holds without GCH.
  - Models saturated over countable subsystems exist when kappa = kappa^aleph_0, without total transcendence.
  - A theory that is not totally transcendental has no countably saturated model of power below 2^aleph_0.
- The editable host n-a-006-01.tex has new attributed remarks at each source location, and its closing questions now state all seven of the source's questions, with (5) as stated in the source.
- Items already drafted in the w03-p03-033 file are cross-referenced there, not rewritten.

Checks:
- unit-compile reports ok. The 3 overfull boxes come from long label-derived annex headings.
- check.py shows no finding for these files. The one hit naming n-a-006-01 is an existing duplicate of annex:p3.morley.stabilization, also defined in n-a-004-02.
- find_fused_spaces is clean.
- No bib keys were added, so no intake bib was created.

Open items:
- The lead must insert this packet's body and annex files and also route the w03-p03-033 files; otherwise the new \cref's in n-a-006-01.tex dangle in main.tex.
- The n. 24 example is constructed only under 2^aleph_0 > aleph_1. The CH case remains open, and the source gives no example.
- The packet lists these units as readonly (owned by w03-p03-033), while the task text assigned the gaps here. None of 033's files were edited.

author.continuation:
The assessment said the owned files do not exist, but that is out of date. A first pass of this block wrote them on 2026-10-11. No driver inputs them or the w03-p03-038 files yet, and that is why a reading of the reader route sees only the host citations. In this pass I re-read the existing written proofs in w03-p03-038 and linked to them instead of duplicating them (A9): the EF theorem (annex:p03-w03-p03-038-pointed-ef) and the cycles distance invariant and response lemma (annex:p03-w03-p03-038-cycle-response, -connectivity). New in this pass, each with a complete annex proof:
- Monotonicity in the number of pebbles, and the pebble relation as an equivalence relation (Kolaitis 2003, p. 56, re-read this session from the scratch text of the online manuscript).
- A new section, sec:p03-w03-p03-055-bounded, on games that bound both rounds and pebbles:
  - the game G^k_m and the relation equiv^k_m;
  - finitely many FO^k formulas of rank m up to equivalence;
  - G^k_m characterizes equiv^k_m;
  - three consequences: equiv^k is agreement for every m and, on finite structures, the unbounded pebble game; with k >= m the game reduces to the EF game; and a definability criterion for FO^k at rank m.
- A 2-colorability result: 2-colorable iff no odd closed walk, defined in L^3_{infty omega}, and Spoiler wins the 3-pebble game for odd m.
- A classification method with side conditions, and a table placing six concepts.
